teaching.hint: What changes in the total when one particular cheese switches recipients?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Assigning everything to one mouse provides a fixed baseline; choosing mouse one changes each item’s contribution independently by its reward difference.
solution_outline.approach: Sum mouse two’s rewards, compute each item’s mouse-one-minus-mouse-two gain, and add the k largest gains.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The baseline is fixed. Each selected index contributes one independent gain, and exactly k indices are selected.
solution_outline.correctness: If a selected gain is smaller than an unselected gain, swapping them preserves the quota and cannot lower the total. Repeating yields the k largest gains.
solution_outline.complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) auxiliary space with sorting; partial selection can improve expected time to O(n).
solution_outline.pitfall: Skipping negative gains violates the exact-k requirement.

common_wrong_turns: Take only positive gains when k requires more
source_fidelity_notes: Retained exact quota including k=0 and k=n; removed answer-specific examples.
